newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK broker group rejects commission cut suggestions.
newsitem.headline: HK broker group rejects commission cut suggestions.

text.p: The Hong Kong Stockbrokers Association said on Wednesday it had rejected the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong's suggestions to introduce negotiable brokerage commissions on large size orders.
"All committee members attending yesterday's (association) meeting unanimously supported to keep the commission structure unchanged," chairman Cheung Tin Sang told Reuters.

The exchange issued a consultation paper to members last month proposing the introduction of a negotiable brokerage commission for orders above HK$3 million, HK$5 million and HK$7 million to enhance competitiveness.
The minimum commission is now 0.25 percent of the value of orders on both the buy and sell side.

The association, which represents about 160 voting members of the exchange, mostly medium- and small-sized brokerage firms, feared that a cut in commissions would mean lower income for medium-sized brokers.

Cheung said a lower brokerage commission may boost business, improving market turnover and trading activity in futures, but added that "only those involved in arbitrage, warrant and index future transactions would benefit if the brokerage commission was cut".
"The proposal of cutting commissions is purely not pragmatic," he said, adding that it had received no demands from local investors to lower commissions.
Cheung said many brokerage firms were charging commission of between 0.3 percent and 0.35 percent. Some even ask as high as 0.5 percent depending on the quality of service provided.
The association said it would inform the exchange by letter of its decision and concerns.
